DECISIONS:
Q1: A
Q2: A

RATIONALE:
Q1: Ubuntu 26.04 ships uutils coreutils, and GitHub is moving `ubuntu-latest` to it gradually between 2026-10-19 and 2026-11-19 (https://github.blog/changelog/2026-09-17-ubuntu-26-generally-available-and-latest-migration/). That explains why the failures look like flakes. It also means all 8 `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` jobs in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and the production workflows will soon run under uutils, so pinning CI (B, A+B) would only hide a production regression. Loosening the tests (C) would drop a contract the repo decided on purpose: AD-4 in `docs/completed/issue-5495-gh-retry-stdout-isolation-plan.md:56,120`, guarded by `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py:228-243`, says output that is not delivered returns non-zero and is never re-run. Fix the scripts and keep the tests as written. In `scripts/gh_helpers.sh` `gh_retry` (lines 1226-1231), the success-path replay must return non-zero when the reader has closed the pipe, without relying on `cat`'s exit status on a broken pipe. It must still never re-run a command that already succeeded. The checkout-head `switch_ms` timing must always produce an integer of milliseconds, whatever the platform's `date` sub-second format support. `switch_ms` is not in this checkout (searched `scripts/`, `tests/` and `.github/` for `*.sh/*.py/*.yml/*.md`, with no match). The planner must find the code that emits it from the failing test's name in the full CI job log, or from the `main`/`ai/issue-9078` code it lives in, and fix it there.
Q2: The fix stays limited to the two failing behaviours, plus any inline `gh_retry` copies in `review_autofix.yml` steps (read by `_inline_gh_retry` in `tests/test_gh_retry_stdout_isolation.py:246`) if they share the same replay path. Those copies are the same function, not new scope. Other uses of `date +%s%3N` (for example `scripts/semble_helpers.sh:95,231,332`, `scripts/review_conflict_resolve.sh:430` and `scripts/build_semble_wrapper.sh:36`) are not covered by failing tests and go to follow-up issues. This change does not touch them. Do not modify or revert PR #9079's CI step moves.
